title: This is wow
author: BellonaSM
selftext:
New world model from Tencent is quite impressive.

I also tested marble 1.1. It was unplesant experience.

https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-World-2.0

comments.author: fungnoth
comments.body: How well does it run locally? VRAM?

replies.author: BellonaSM
replies.body: I have 3090 and middle of testing will comment how much vram required

replies.author: BellonaSM
replies.body: Ok just tested it. Current open version is 3d reconstruction gsplat only. It is quite quick and you can run with local gpu.

comments.author: PensionSeveral4041
comments.body: Still don’t understand the point. It’s a 3d character moving in a Gaussian splatting environment with faked perspective and colliders. What is the goal with that?

replies.author: JjyKs
replies.body:
From their Git:  
  
`Unlike video-only world models (e.g., Genie 3, HY World 1.5), HY-World 2.0 generates real 3D assets — 3DGS, meshes, and point clouds — that are freely explorable, editable, and directly importable into Unity / Unreal Engine / Isaac.`

I also see the point in video only models as well. We're really far from it, but in theory nothing blocks the AI from simulating and remembering the whole world. Imagine a "game" that just keeps on going forever and allows you to do whatever you want.

replies.author: PensionSeveral4041
replies.body:
Well. It’s a 3D character that moves in a Gaussian splatting environment. Even exported to Unity, what are you mean to do with it?

All these models come with a “imagine” promise, that never goes further than a random character in third person moving in a fisheye camera angle background.

replies.author: Derefringence
replies.body: Think beyond entertainment, these world sim technologies are being used to generate training data for autonomous robots

replies.author: Gubzs
replies.body: It's a step toward locally generating something more detailed and useful. Progress is iterative.

comments.author: Ludagon
comments.body:
Interesting. I've been doing a fair bit of gaussian splatting of real world places into Unity as game environments recently, manually layering splats, mesh colliders off adjacent photogrammetry techniques, etc.  
The results are awesome but there's so much manual handling in my current workflow to make it work well.

Keen to test this out and see if I can do the processing into splats locally instead of paying a cloud photogrammetry processing service, and if it can line up the world colliders in a Unity-friendly way then that's very cool indeed.

Thanks for sharing :)
